newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly up amid consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly up amid consolidation.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly higher on Wednesday amid continued profit-taking pressure, but brokers said the index may have a chance to challenge resistance at 7,000 points on Thursday.
The weighted index ended 7.25 points or a scant 0.10 percent higher at 6,943.64. Turnover was a modest T$75 billion, sharply down from Tuesday's hectic T$125.9 billion.

The market did not respond immediately to surprise plans by Singapore's SIMEX exchange to launch Taiwan stock index futures and options in January, but brokers said this was seen as positive news in the long term.
"The market was under the shadow of yesterday's profit-taking and the overnight fall on Wall Street during most of the session," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
"There should be a more positive response as more investors find out the (SIMEX) news tomorrow," Lin said.
"The plans by CME and SIMEX will bring more foreign funds into the market next year. The outlook is quite bullish."
The U.S. Commodities Futures Trading Commission in November approved similar plans by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange to list futures and futures option contracts linked to Taiwan stocks.
Electronic shares were weak. Recently listed "king share" Asustek plunged by the daily seven percent limit to T$306. The king share is that with the highest price stock in the market.
Likewise, newcomer Inventec Corp was limit down to T$164.
Both Asustek and Inventec were listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in early November and had soared for several sessions in what brokers called a honeymoon rally.
Newly listed bank share United World Chinese Commercial Bank rose T$5 or 6.67 percent to T$80.
